survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD Survey of Adult Skills country note reports results from a nationally representative household survey of adults aged 16–65 in Norway (2022–23). The sample was drawn to be representative of the target population (about 3.6 million adults aged 16–65) and analyses were conducted to check that non-response would not introduce significant bias. The note does not specify the exact survey weight variable names or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For analysts using the underlying Survey of Adult Skills microdata, complex survey design features (stratification/clustering and non-response adjustments) should be respected when estimating means, proficiency levels, and regression-based associations.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The document is a country note summarizing proficiency distributions and associations; it does not report an explicit plausible-values (PV) workflow or missing-data handling procedure for an empirical student-level predictive model. While the Survey of Adult Skills uses proficiency estimation based on task success/failure, the note does not describe whether PVs were generated/combined or how missing responses were imputed/deleted. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not documented at the level required for extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the Norway 2022–23 Survey of Adult Skills Second Cycle country sample. The note states that the sample was drawn to be representative of adults aged 16–65 residing in Norway and that analyses were conducted to assess non-response bias. It also describes an assessment-language accommodation: some participants not sufficiently fluent received a doorstep questionnaire, and doorstep respondents are generally excluded when comparing across cycles; the note indicates such exclusions are applied for comparability across cycles.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for Norway summarizes adult proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—assessed in 2022–23 among adults aged 16–65 (n=4,053; response rate 41%). Proficiency is reported on 500-point scales with discrete proficiency levels (e.g., Level 1 or below; Levels 4–5), and uncertainty is shown via 95% confidence intervals around mean estimates. Norway’s mean performance is above the OECD average in all three domains (literacy 281, numeracy 285, adaptive problem solving 271). The note reports distributional shares at low and high proficiency levels, age-related gaps (older adults lower than 25–34-year-olds), and trends since the first participation in 2011–12 (numeracy improved; literacy broadly stable). It also describes associations between higher numeracy proficiency and labour force participation, unemployment risk, wages, and well-being/civic outcomes, while excluding doorstep-only respondents in some comparisons for cross-cycle comparability.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD country note that reports descriptive proficiency results and regression-based associations rather than an ML predictive modeling study. As such, there is no student-level machine learning pipeline to extract (no algorithms, no PV-combination method, and no missing-data strategy for an ML model). The extraction therefore leaves ML-specific fields empty and focuses on assessment design and reported proficiency/association outcomes.
